deviations.what: Report artifacts move to one subdirectory PER RUN — data/reports/<verb>/<run-id>/ — instead of loose files in a shared flat directory. t5 built write_artifact_set to replace an entire destination directory, which is the correct primitive only if that directory belongs to a single run. t7 discovered the mismatch (a shared flat directory legitimately holds sibling reports, and a directory-level swap would delete them, with a race under pytest -n auto) and fell back to two unprotected sequential writes — which is precisely the hazard h31 forbids: a complete CSV beside a missing or stale HTML. The user chose the per-run subdirectory layout, which makes t5's single os.replace genuinely atomic as built rather than weakening the guarantee.
deviations.reason: t5's API and the shared-directory layout are incompatible; t7's fallback silently dropped the all-or-nothing guarantee that c35/h31 requires. Per-run subdirectories resolve it in favour of the guarantee instead of against it.

deviations.what: The links extraction cache is written to a SIBLING run directory named <run-id>-cache, not into the run's own report directory. write_artifact_set replaces its entire destination directory with exactly the file set it is handed, so the report set (HTML + 2 CSVs) and the cache cannot share one run directory — whichever wrote second would delete the first. t10 could not extend jlab/links/cache.py (t9's file), so it added a module-level _cache_run_id() helper in the CLI instead. --from-cache accepts either spelling.
deviations.reason: d1's per-run-directory layout makes write_artifact_set atomic, but it also means one directory holds exactly one artifact set. The cache is a second set. Neither t9 nor t10 owned both files needed to resolve it cleanly.

deviations.what: A cache-rendered links report carries NO coverage figures. write_cache's payload is {scanned_at, records} — the scan's per-channel ok/partial/failed statuses are not in it. t10 passes a minimal scan_result so the metadata renders coverage as 'unknown' and says coverage is incomplete, rather than inventing numbers. This diverges from t9's acceptance line 'rendering from the cache produces the same report and CSVs as the run that wrote it': the link rows and tables are identical, the coverage cells are not.
deviations.reason: The gap was discovered wiring the two together; closing it requires caching the coverage fields alongside the records, which is a change in jlab/links/cache.py — a file t10 did not own.

deltas.behavior_text: Report artifacts land in a per-run subdirectory (data/reports/<verb>/<run-id>/) instead of loose files in a shared directory. This changes the output path of the already-shipped jlab discord members verb, and is what makes each run's whole set land through a single atomic os.replace.

The links extraction cache is written to a sibling <run-id>-cache directory rather than the run's own, because write_artifact_set replaces its entire destination directory and one run directory therefore holds exactly one artifact set. --from-cache accepts either spelling.

The cache payload carries a trimmed copy of the scan's six coverage fields alongside the records, so a cached re-render states real coverage instead of unknown. A payload lacking the key still loads and falls back to unknown.

Extraction reads embed description and field bodies as a fourth source, not just embeds[].url. The t1 probe measured that auto-preview embeds duplicate a URL already in content while rich embeds carry url=None and hide links in the body, so embeds[].url alone would have added duplicates and still missed the unreachable links.

Attachment URLs are never rendered as clickable anchors at all, regardless of scheme — stronger than the specced 'marked as expiring'. They render as monospace text with an EXPIRING badge and the jump link beside them as the clickable route back.
